messages.author: 72ea92d72402d82e
messages.subject: Problems with dlply & lm
parts:
HI All,

I've got a data set where I would like to apply linear regression to
subsets of my data. My data is set up as the following:

Bioassay=
Site Month Year Day DOC
1 0 1 2007 1 2.7
2 0 1 2007 4 2.5
3 0 1 2007 7 2.3
4 125 1 2007 1 3.0
5 125 1 2007 5 3.0
6 125 1 2007 10 3.0
7 225 2 2008 0 3.1
8 225 2 2008 2 3.0
9 225 2 2008 8 2.9

I would like to run a linear regression of DOC by Day, where my data
is split up by Site, Month, and Year. I realize that with the above
data set, I could just split by site - this is an abbreviated data
set, the data set I need to work with is much larger, and has more
overlap between Site, Month, and Year.

I set up my function as follows:

linmodel<-function(linmod){
lm(DOC ~ Day, data=Bioassay)}
linear<-dlply(Bioassay, .(Year, Month, Site), linmodel)
lin.coef <- ldply(linear, function(linmod) c(coef(linmod)))

And what I get in return is:

Year Month Site (Intercept) Day
1 2007 1 0 2.904018 -0.01674107
2 2007 1 125 2.904018 -0.01674107
3 2008 2 225 2.904018 -0.01674107

As you can see, my intercept and coefficients are all the same. The
lm function is taking into account all of my data & I know that the
intercept and coefficients are NOT the same given Site, Month, and
Year (I get the same outcome with lm(DOC ~ Day, data=Bioassay).

Given all of the examples I have found online and also referencing
Hadley Wickham's paper in the Journal of Statistical Software, I can't
figure out where I'm going wrong with this.

Any hints/helpful comments would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you
Amber Ulseth

messages.author: e531efa2753b204e
messages.subject: Re: Problems with dlply & lm
parts:
On Fri, Nov 18, 2011 at 3:24 PM, AJU <amber....@gmail.com> wrote:
> linmodel<-function(linmod){
>        lm(DOC ~ Day, data=Bioassay)}

The argument to linmodel here is unused -- you're handing all of
Bioassay to lm each time, which explains your problem. So change this
to:

linmodel<-function(data){
       lm(DOC ~ Day, data=data)
}

Peter,

Thank you! That did it. I changed the function as you suggested to:

linmodel<-function(Bioassay){

lm(DOC ~ Day, data=Bioassay)}
linear<-dlply(Bioassay, .(Year, Month, Site), linmodel)
lin.coef <- ldply(linear, function(linmod) c(coef(linmod)))

where 'Bioassay' is the name of my data.

2 2007 1 125 3.000000 -8.196234e-17
3 2008 2 225 3.076923 -2.307692e-02


Thank you!

Best,
Amber
